title: Three-Payment Settlement Recorded-Call Acceptance: The First-Payment Window
content:
# Three-Payment Settlement — Call Acceptance Window

The Three-Payment call acceptance window is the number of calendar days from the acceptance date to the due date of the first settlement payment when a consumer accepts a Three-Payment Settlement offer of Ridgeline's Settlement Agreements on a recorded call.

## Definition

1. **The offered Three-Payment window** is the number of calendar days from the offer date of that open offer to the first payment due date written on it, never more than 15 days.
2. **The Three-Payment call acceptance window** is the offered Three-Payment window, never less than one day.
3. **On acceptance** the first settlement payment falls due that many calendar days after the acceptance date, each later payment falls due the offer's payment interval after the one before it, and the offer's settlement amount is booked to the settlement once, on the acceptance date.

The window is formed once: the offered window is capped at 15 days, any shortenings of the call window that apply are taken together and subtracted from it in one step, and the figure is never less than one day.

## Worked example on hypothetical figures

| Item | Hypothetical figure |
|---|---|
| Offer date of the open Three-Payment offer | day X |
| First payment due date written on the offer | day X plus 15 |
| Offered Three-Payment window | 15 days, not above the 15-day cap |
| Call acceptance window | 15 days |
| Acceptance on the recorded call | day Y |
| Payment 1 / 2 / 3 due (30-day interval) | day Y plus 15 / Y plus 45 / Y plus 75 |
| Settlement amount booked | once, on day Y |

## Points of judgement

- **From which date are the days counted on acceptance?** From the acceptance date, not from the offer date.
- **Can an offered window written on an offer exceed 15 days in the call window?** No; the offered window is never taken as more than 15 days.
- **How often is the settlement amount booked?** Once, on the acceptance date.
